dazdiff

dazdiff compares two tables value by value and returns one row per compared value, traced back to its source row in both tables.

  • It can test a table against a benchmark whose column types are the truth: the tested table’s columns are cast to those types and its column names normalized, so a table that went through a database or Spark compares with the one that went in.
  • Rows are paired on their identity columns, never by position, and a key that repeats is reported rather than silently paired.
  • Its one dependency outside base R is data.table.

Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("dazdiff")

Or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/dazdiff")

Usage

A table, and the same data after a round trip through storage: the names changed case, the ids became text, one amount moved and one row was replaced. diff_table() pairs the rows on id and compares amount:

library(dazdiff)

benchmark <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(100, 200, 300))
stored <- data.frame(ID = c("1", "2", "4"), Amount = c(100, 200.5, 400))

diff_table(benchmark, stored, by = "id")
#> Key: <ID, metric>
#>       ID metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff    rel_diff  status
#>    <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>       <num>  <fctr>
#> 1:     1 AMOUNT        1        1     100   100.0   0.0      0.0 0.000000000    same
#> 2:     2 AMOUNT        2        2     200   200.5   0.5      0.5 0.002493766 changed
#> 3:     3 AMOUNT        3       NA     300      NA    NA       NA          NA  only_x
#> 4:     4 AMOUNT       NA        3      NA   400.0    NA       NA          NA  only_y

Column names are normalized to upper case, which is how id pairs with ID. status says what happened to each value, and row_id_x and row_id_y are its rows in the two tables.

dazdiff also summarizes and draws a comparison, finds which keys hold the differences, compares two tables as equals, and works as a testthat expectation. Get started shows each of these.
